name: Before and after metric card

structure.anatomy: Frame splits vertically. Starting number left, desired number right, a divider or arrow between them. Labels sit small under each figure. Product attribution is a single line at the base. No qualifier language anywhere.

whyItWorks: The gap between the two numbers does the persuading. Nothing has to be claimed, the reader does the subtraction themselves and arrives at the conclusion unaided.
gtAngle: Left is the constraint today, right is the same number after the fix, with the engine dollar range as the divider. This is the one format that shows what Growth Terminal is actually selling, the delta, rather than describing it.
novelty: no close match in the bank

name: Report cover, lead magnet

structure.anatomy: Composition mimics a printed industry report. Oversized title, a single branded object centred, production quality doing the persuading. Download CTA at the base. Deliberately editorial rather than promotional.

whyItWorks: Perceived production value transfers to perceived substance before a word is read. A generic template reads as filler, a designed cover reads as research worth an email address.
gtAngle: The intelligence briefing and the state of growth reviews research already exist on the site and have no ad format pointing at them. This is a distribution layout for assets that are already written.
novelty: no close match in the bank

name: Behaviour call out

structure.anatomy: Small icon or illustration anchors one side. A single line names a specific thing the reader already does. A stat or qualifier sits below it. The CTA asks for something the reader already possesses rather than a commitment.

whyItWorks: Naming a behaviour the reader recognises in themselves earns the next two seconds. The ask is low friction because it requests something already in hand.
gtAngle: Growth Terminal reads a spreadsheet the reader already has open. The ask is literally a file they already own, which is exactly the low friction shape this format is built for.
novelty: no close match in the bank

name: Proprietary data insight

structure.anatomy: A branded chart carrying an insight only this company could produce. Minimal supporting text. The visualization is both the proof and the product demonstration at once.

whyItWorks: The product generates the data and the data becomes the advertisement. It cannot be copied by a competitor because they do not have the dataset.
gtAngle: The engine has run analyses across twelve constraint categories. Which constraint bites most often, and at what severity, is a number nobody else can publish. This is the strongest long term format on the list because it compounds as more analyses run.
novelty: no close match in the bank

name: Event or live session

structure.anatomy: A coloured pill label sets urgency at the top. Faces with titles occupy the centre. A branded object backs the composition. Date and time anchor the base. CTA drives registration rather than purchase.

whyItWorks: A real deadline plus a human face create time pressure and social proof in the same frame, without either being claimed in copy.
gtAngle: Only worth building when there is a real session to run. Filed so the shape exists when it is needed, not before.
novelty: no close match in the bank

name: Case study metric with customer logo

structure.anatomy: An outcome statement, a recognisable customer logo directly beneath, restrained typography, one CTA, no secondary copy at all.

whyItWorks: The logo validates the claim before the reader has time to form an objection. Peer credibility outranks any brand assertion.
gtAngle: BLOCKED, not unbuilt. This format needs a named customer willing to be shown with a real number. Building the layout before that exists would mean inventing one. Revisit when the first customer agrees to be named.
novelty: no close match in the bank

name: Giant metric typography

structure.anatomy: One oversized number occupies more than half the frame. A short context line sits under it. Branding is small. Legible at thumbnail scale, functions as a billboard.

whyItWorks: Scale alone stops the scroll. The number is readable before the reader has decided whether to read.
gtAngle: The bank already has stat. Worth checking whether stat pushes the number far enough, since this variant is specifically about billboard scale rather than a number with supporting copy.
novelty: variant of stat

name: Bold headline over product UI

structure.anatomy: Headline owns the upper third, product screenshot fills the lower half, often device framed. Logo small in a corner, one CTA anchoring the base.

whyItWorks: The headline does not make a claim, it shows one. Visual and verbal aligned on the same use case turn the ad into evidence.
gtAngle: Already added as the highlight layout, built from the Owner ad. Parked as confirmation the shape was worth taking.
novelty: variant of highlight

name: Metric first social proof

structure.anatomy: Large display metric centred, customer attribution directly beneath, brand and CTA in a footer bar.

whyItWorks: A verifiable figure tied to a named source feels testable in a way a generic outcome claim never does.
gtAngle: Variant of stat. Blocked by the same missing ingredient as the case study format, a named customer.
novelty: variant of stat

name: Product UI as hero

structure.anatomy: Interface occupies nearly the whole frame, text minimal, headline and logo in opposite corners, dark background receding.

whyItWorks: When the product design is self explanatory the workflow is recognised instantly by the right operator and ignored by everyone else, which is efficient targeting.
gtAngle: prodshot covers this. Parked.
novelty: variant of prodshot

name: Pattern interrupt

structure.anatomy: One striking image that breaks the category visual template. Strikethrough text, unexpected colour, or a visual joke. Minimal copy, plain CTA.

whyItWorks: Contrast against the feed does the scroll stopping before any text registers.
gtAngle: contrast and statement cover the typographic version. The meme version is off brand for a diagnostic tool and would cost more credibility than it buys.
novelty: variant of contrast

name: Executive quote stack

structure.anatomy: Quote occupies the primary real estate. Name, title and company logo stack below it. Surrounding visual kept deliberately quiet.

whyItWorks: A verifiable attributed claim outranks anything the brand says about itself.
gtAngle: quote layout already exists. Needs real attributed quotes before it should run.
novelty: variant of quote

name: Live product demo with odd number

structure.anatomy: Screenshot of the product mid task, carrying a deliberately non round number. Minimal headline.

whyItWorks: Specificity reads as real customer data. A round number reads as an illustration, an odd one reads as a screenshot.
gtAngle: Worth borrowing as a rule rather than a layout: dollar ranges in creatives should be odd, matching what the engine actually returns.
novelty: variant of prodshot

name: Compressed dual claim headline

structure.anatomy: Under ten words carrying both a magnitude and a speed claim at equal weight.

whyItWorks: It answers how much and how fast in one line, closing the two most common objections simultaneously.
gtAngle: A copy rule rather than a layout. The size of the constraint plus about sixty seconds is exactly this shape, and it belongs in the hook pools rather than in a new renderer.
novelty: variant of statement

name: Localized or vertical messaging

structure.anatomy: One visual treatment held constant while the headline carries a regional or vertical marker.

whyItWorks: Signals the ad was made for this specific reader rather than broadcast, at almost no production cost.
gtAngle: Not a layout, a variant axis. The industry playbook pages already exist for agency, ecommerce, saas, b2b services, coaching and local services, so the copy already exists to feed it.
novelty: no close match in the bank

name: Three stage pipeline, reports to analysis to decision

structure.anatomy: Three panels in sequence with arrows between. Panel one: the messy input, a spreadsheet of too much data, deliberately illegible. Panel two: the analysis, a clean metric table with ONE row ringed in brand colour, showing current vs benchmark vs gap vs impact. Panel three: the decision, a bordered verdict card with a directive (FIX THIS FIRST), the specific action, and one large money figure. The persuasion is the transformation: chaos becomes one ringed row becomes one instruction with a number.

whyItWorks: It shows the product doing its job instead of describing it. The ringed row is the product moment. The reader follows the arrows and experiences the compression from 40 numbers to 1 decision.
gtAngle: This IS the GT flow: paste the sheet, the engine ranks constraints against benchmarks, one gets named and priced, the verdict card says fix this first.

novelty: no close match in the bank

name: unique positioning statement

structure.anatomy: headline defines the unique value proposition in under 10 words

whyItWorks: It captures what makes a business valuable and differentiates it in the client's mind, ensuring it stands out in a crowded market. Evidence: Positioning is the process of differentiating a product, service or company in the customer’s mind to obtain a strategic competitive advantage
gtAngle: a tool could assess the clarity and uniqueness of the positioning statement against competitors

name: client-centric value identification

structure.anatomy: list of client problems solved is presented in bullet points

whyItWorks: It emphasizes understanding client needs and how the business can uniquely solve their problems, which builds stronger connections and loyalty. Evidence: Speed: Your turnaround times are low, and for the right fee, you could make yourself available on short notice
gtAngle: a tool could evaluate the relevance of identified client problems to the target audience

name: specific link text

structure.anatomy: link text must be descriptive and unique for different URLs

whyItWorks: Specific link text provides clarity and context for users, especially those using screen readers, which improves accessibility and reduces friction in the buying process. Evidence: 73.73% of marketing emails have no discernible link text, forcing screen reader users to guess where links lead
gtAngle: this can be used to assess the clarity of link text in emails and product pages

name: short sentences

structure.anatomy: sentences should be capped at 20 words

whyItWorks: Short sentences enhance readability and comprehension, making it easier for all users, including those using screen readers, to process information quickly and effectively. Evidence: The British Government's content team found that reader understanding drops off sharply after 25-29 words
gtAngle: this can be used to evaluate the length of sentences in product descriptions and emails

name: corn fed analogy

structure.anatomy: uses a strong metaphor to connect product positioning with animal feeding practices

whyItWorks: The article uses the analogy of corn-fed animals to illustrate the dangers of artificially boosting product positioning with excessive marketing spend, making the concept relatable and memorable. Evidence: The article states that 40% of cows will die if fed corn instead of grass, highlighting the risks of poor positioning strategies.
gtAngle: This analogy can be used to diagnose whether a company's marketing strategy is sustainable or artificially inflated.

name: extreme product makeover

structure.anatomy: provides specific examples of successful product transformations

whyItWorks: The article emphasizes the success of extreme product makeovers for brands like Folgers and Pampers, showcasing a proven method for revitalizing stagnant sales. Evidence: Folgers, Pampers, and Tylenol became billion-dollar product lines after undergoing makeovers, demonstrating the effectiveness of this strategy.
gtAngle: This finding can help identify brands that may benefit from a similar makeover approach.

name: data architecture audit

structure.anatomy: headline suggests a critical first step in platform evaluation

whyItWorks: The article emphasizes the importance of auditing current data architecture to identify fragmentation before selecting an enterprise marketing automation platform. Evidence: If the answer is 'three or more places,' your first purchase criterion should be unified data rather than feature count.
gtAngle: This could be used to guide organizations in assessing their data management practices before investing in new tools.

name: cross-channel orchestration

structure.anatomy: call to action for vendors to demonstrate capabilities

whyItWorks: The article highlights the necessity for enterprise marketing platforms to coordinate multiple channels from a single canvas, which enhances campaign effectiveness. Evidence: ask vendors to demonstrate a live orchestration flow that includes at least three channels and a conditional branch based on account-level data.
gtAngle: This can help organizations evaluate the integration capabilities of marketing platforms.

name: Guest Teaching

structure.anatomy: headline emphasizes the benefit of borrowing trust from established communities

whyItWorks: It allows you to borrow the trust of an established community, reaching eager, ready-to-buy people who have already invested in solving their problems. Evidence: Jess Haney, a SaaS copywriter, stated that leading trainings inside group coaching programs has been one of the fastest and most consistent ways that I’ve gotten clients.
gtAngle: Create an ad promoting a guest teaching opportunity in a paid community targeting your ideal clients.

name: Podcast Guesting

structure.anatomy: headline highlights the long-term benefits of podcast guesting for lead generation

whyItWorks: It leverages the host's credibility and audience, creating a stacking effect of exposure that builds trust over time. Evidence: Abi Prendergast mentioned that podcasts have been the single best lead gen source for her, leading to clients at 10, 20, and 50K price points directly from a podcast.
gtAngle: Design an ad campaign showcasing the benefits of being a podcast guest for lead generation.

name: Upgrade Announcement

structure.anatomy: headline highlights the major upgrade and its benefits in under 10 words

whyItWorks: Announcing a major upgrade creates excitement and urgency among users, encouraging them to explore new features and improvements. Evidence: SparkToro's V3 is the 3rd major iteration since the product's first launch in 2020.
gtAngle: Create a launch ad that emphasizes the new features and improvements of SparkToro V3.

name: brand affinity data

structure.anatomy: headline clearly states the new feature and its purpose in under 10 words

whyItWorks: This feature allows marketers to understand which brands their audience is familiar with, enhancing targeting and content strategies. Evidence: The new Brand Affinity section can be found in the Keywords and Prompts dropdown.
gtAngle: Create an ad showcasing how brand affinity data can improve marketing strategies for agencies.
